doc.cr_project.int__booking_forecast.name: int__booking_forecast
doc.cr_project.int__booking_forecast.block_contents:
This model is the current mapping area for Project Forecasting that utilizes Workday Forecasted Hours via the Workday API EXT_PROJECT_RESOURCE_FORECAST
        The name of this model could be changed, as there are other non-forecast hour Forecast methods

        The main mapping that occurs is:
        - contract_rate_sheets via stg_workday__contract_rate_sheet, to see whether Project Rate is Daily or Weekly
        - contract_rate_sheets_override via stg_workday__contract_rate_sheet_override, to see whether a Workday/Project Contract Rate override exists
        - Mappings to other Business Concepts via the Project_BK
        - The Project's attributes (Especially the Deal/SOW) value
        - Various issue flags to see whether the project is in an invliad state
        - This logic could easily be migrated into the opportunity exposure mode
        
        As per February 2025, 
        the cost center in the forecast bookings refers to the cost centre in workday rather in salesforce

        As per March 2026,
        This model now filters `bc_forecast_booking` to only include the most current version of each forecast record
        (`current_timestamp() between effective_from and effective_to`), as historical cost rate tracking (SCD2 behaviour)
        is not required for utilisation or project profitability reporting.

doc.cr_project.int_project_forecast.name: int_project_forecast
doc.cr_project.int_project_forecast.block_contents:
This view contains the Project Forecasted Hours from the Workday Project Resource Forecast(via Datavault models).
        Uses the Actual Tracker to determine which months are Forecast vs Actuals.

        As per March 2026,
        This model now filters `bc_forecast_booking` to only include the most current version of each forecast record
        (`current_timestamp() between effective_from and effective_to`), as historical cost rate tracking (SCD2 behaviour)
        is not required for utilisation or project profitability reporting.

doc.cr_project.int__booking_forecast__fi.name: int__booking_forecast__fixed_price
doc.cr_project.int__booking_forecast__fi.block_contents:
This view contains forecasting data for Professional Services/Tesltra Purple - Fixed Price - Closed Won Projects
      As a PS Fixed Price project has no 'Contract Rates', the 'Remaining Deal Value' of the project is split proportionally between the months and then hours assigned to the project

      Concepts used:
        - Deal Value
        - Actual Tracker (Which montsh are Forecast vs Actuals)
        - Actuals
        - Remaining Deal Value = 'Deal Value' - 'Finalised Actuals'
        - Forecasted Hours grouped by month

      This 'Remaining Deal Value' is split into the remaining Forecast months as per the Actuals Tracker, and then further into the hours assigned into each month, providing each month an hourly rate we can apply to assigned hours

      E.g.:
        $1000 Remaining for 2 months on a project
        Month 1: 10 hours total
        Month 1: 20 hours total
        Total Month Count: 2
        Monthly Amount: $1000 / 2 = $500

        Month 1: $500 -> $500 / 10 hours = $50 hourly rate
        Month 2: $500 -> $100 / 20 Hours = $25 hourly Rate

        As per 14/8/2025, the filter of business unit has been changed to cost center bk to create more robustness on the data when the businness unit name changes
        Included 12 cost centers that are within Professional Services and pruple C&D business units which are 
        'CC100', 'CC101','CC102','CC103','CC104','CC105','CC106','CC107','CC108','CC800','CC801','CC802'

        The cost center filter is the employee's cost center thus the joins with bc_employee and bc_cost center because it allows the utils to i
        include VMS project that are done by Professional Services and Purple poeple .
        
        As per October 2025, 
        All the historical records of the project role cost rate are now included with the respective effective from and effective to dates. 

        As per March 2026,
        A `resource_forecast_bk` column has been added to uniquely identify each forecast booking line.
        This is sourced from `bc_forecast_booking.resource_forecast_bk` via `int_project_forecast`,
        which is itself derived from the Workday project resource forecast line identifier.

doc.cr_project.int__booking_forecast__fi.name: int__booking_forecast__fixed_price__normalised_spread
doc.cr_project.int__booking_forecast__fi.block_contents:
This model recieves a list of Opportunities/Projects with a custom Start_Date, End_Date and Value attached
        The model then splits the remaining value of the project, in a monthly granularity, between the start and end date

        Considerations taken into account:
          - The first and last months only forecast for the days in teh month that are between the Start and End Date
          - Every month is normalised and is calculated as if it were 30 days. This is so that a 28 day month and a 31 day monthe ach recieve the same revenue
          - int__booking_forecast__fixed_price__normalised_spread__projects allows for custom Start Date, End Date and value, meaning that the model is Salesfore/Workday agnostic

        As per March 2026,
        A `resource_forecast_bk` column has been added to uniquely identify each forecast booking line.
        It is generated as `OPPORTUNITY_BK || '|' || DATE_BK`, combining the opportunity and date to form a unique key per project-month.

doc.cr_project.int__booking_forecast__fi.name: int__booking_forecast__fixed_price__normalised_spread__projects
doc.cr_project.int__booking_forecast__fi.block_contents:
This view obtains Projects that are to be used in the int__booking_forecast__fixed_price__normalised_spread model
        They are provided in a seperate model as to allow for easy troubleshooting on filtering
        The view also allwos for the custom mapping of the following fields, based on the Forecast Method's requirements
          - Opportunity/Project Start Date
          - Opportunity/Project End Date
          - Opportunity/Project Value

        These project types are currently for:
         - Time & Materials projects that are missing a Contract Rate Sheet
            - Replaces T&M Rates * Hours with the Salesforce SOW amount
         - [ONCE APPROVED] VMS Projects

doc.cr_project.int__booking_forecast__fi.name: int__booking_forecast__fixed_price__monthly_rates
doc.cr_project.int__booking_forecast__fi.block_contents:
This model calculates how much a Professional Servcies Fixed Price project ('Prof Serve: FP') should charge per hour for a project
        The main outputs are the project code, and the MONTH_HOURLY_RATE of each PROJECT_BK/MONTH_START_DATE
        Whilst Fixed Price Projects don't have an hourly rate attached, revenue is recognised on a Forecasted Hour basis and so an Hourly rate per month is required to proportionally forecast the amount recieved

        This month hourly rate is calculated by:
          1) Taking all Forecasted Hours, calculating the proportion of hours in a single month vs the total ()
          2) Receiving the Remaining Deal Value (Deal_Value - Actuals)
          3) Multiplying the remaining Deal_Value against this monthly proportion to obtain Monthly_Revenue
          4) Divide this Monthly_Revenue by the hours in the month to obtain the MONTH_HOURLY_RATE that can then be multiplied against Forecasted Hours

        Model Specific Inputs:
          PROJECT_BK
          MONTH_START_DATE
          FORECASTED_HOURS_MONTH
          REMAINING_FORECAST_HOURS
          REMAINING_DEAL_VALUE

        Model Specific Outputs:
          PROJECT_BK
          MONTH_START_DATE
          MONTH_HOURLY_RATE

doc.cr_project.int__booking_forecast__ti.name: int__booking_forecast__time_and_materials
doc.cr_project.int__booking_forecast__ti.block_contents:
This model provides forecasting for Workday projects with a PRIMARY_PROJECT_HIERARCHY of Prof Serve: TM
      The Forecasting is based on the Workday API EXT_PROJECT_RESOURCE_FORECAST, as bases forecasting on Forecasted Hours and a Worker's Contract Rate on said specific Project
      The calculation is done via:

      - Seeing whether an 'Override rate' has been applied, and use this if provided
      - Multiply the worker's Rate by the Hours on a project/day, and the Daily revenue is provided

      If a Contract Rate Sheet is not applied, 0 revenue would be provided. A seperate model 'int__booking_forecast__fixed_price__normalised_spread__projects' provides backup forecasting in this case

    As per October 2025, 
    All the historical records of the project role cost rate are now included with the respective effective from and effective to dates.

doc.cr_project.int__booking_forecast__ti.name: int__booking_forecast__time_and_materials__all_stages
doc.cr_project.int__booking_forecast__ti.block_contents:
The int__booking_forecast__time_and_materials model requires only projects that are in a 'CLOSED_WON' stage
      Finance are required to see T&M projects of all stages to assist in reconciliation
      This model allows for the T&M calculations to be exposed to finance, and then only 'CLOSED_WON' projects to be filtered in the next model

      Materialized to table since exposure parents are expected to be tables or incremental view.

doc.cr_project.int_fact_project_revenue_.block_contents:
# Model: int_fact_project_revenue__bks

## Business Purpose
Creates an intermediate layer that assembles business keys and performs necessary transformations for the project revenue fact table.
This model enriches journal line data with opportunity relationships, applies exchange rate conversions, and resolves client attribution logic.

## Business Logic & Key Calculations

### Exchange Rate Conversion
- Applies average exchange rates from `bc_exchange_rates` to convert all amounts to AUD
- Joins on date and source currency to find applicable rate
- Revenue amount calculation: `(ledger_budget_debit_minus_credit * exchange_rate) * -1`
- Rounds to 2 decimal places as NUMBER(18,2)

### Revenue Category Mapping
- Primary source: `bridge_project_revenue.revenue_category_bk`
- Fallback: Maps from spend category using `stg_manual_spend_category_revenue_category`
- Uses manual mapping when revenue category is 'ghost'

### Data Filtering
- **Only includes Posted journal lines** (`status = 'Posted'`)
- Excludes cancelled transactions

## Sources & Dependencies

### Direct Dependencies
- `dvbridge_project_revenue` - Links to dimensions (journal, region, project, cost center, practice, client, revenue category, sales item, account, company, spend category)
- `bc_project_revenue` - Core revenue transaction data with amounts and metadata
- `dvbridge_opportunity_project` - Links projects to opportunities
- `dvbridge_opportunity` - Opportunity details including client and account director
- `bc_exchange_rates` - Currency conversion rates (filtered to AUD target, Average rate type)
- `stg_manual_spend_category_revenue_category` - Manual mapping between spend and revenue categories

## Key Fields

### Grain
- `project_revenue_bk` - Unique identifier for each revenue transaction

### Measures
- `revenue_amount` - Converted AUD amount (posted transactions only)
- `exchange_rate` - Applied conversion rate
- `currency` - Original transaction currency

### Attributes
- `operational_transaction`, `header_memo`, `line_memo` - Transaction details
- `source`, `record_source` - Data lineage
- `status` - Journal status (filtered to 'Posted')
- `exchange_rate_effective_from`, `exchange_rate_effective_to` - Rate validity period

## Additional Notes
- Ghost records are used for missing optional relationships
- All revenue amounts are standardized to AUD for consistent reporting
- Complex client attribution logic supports both direct journal entries and opportunity-linked projects
- Manual revenue category mapping provides flexibility for unmapped spend categories

doc.cr_project.int_fact_project_revenue.name: int_fact_project_revenue

# Model: int_fact_project_revenue

## Business Purpose
Transforms business keys from `int_fact_project_revenue__bks` into surrogate keys (SIDs) following the data warehouse naming standards.
This model serves as the final preparation layer before the fact table, ensuring all dimensional references use hashed surrogate keys.
## Sources & Dependencies

### Direct Dependencies

### Downstream Usage

## Key Fields

- Dimension SIDs hashed from corresponding business keys
- All dimensional references converted to binary surrogate keys for fact table joins

### Measures & Attributes
- Inherits all measures and attributes from `int_fact_project_revenue__bks`
- Field names standardized to match data warehouse conventions

## Update Frequency
Refreshed with dbt run schedule, in sync with `int_fact_project_revenue__bks`.

## Additional Notes
- This is a thin transformation layer focused solely on key standardization
- All business logic resides in `int_fact_project_revenue__bks`
- Follows data warehouse pattern of separating business key assembly from surrogate key generation

doc.cr_project.int_fact_time_sheet__bks.block_contents:
This model sources all business keys and attributes directly from `bc_time_sheet`, which now contains the latest timesheet records and all required fields.

## Key Features
- Uses `bc_time_sheet` for both business keys and attributes (project, employee, cost center, practice, project role, etc.)
- Joins timesheet records to client dimension via project and opportunity bridge tables
- Enriches timesheets with cost rates from `bc_project_cost_rate` based on:
  - Employee assignment
  - Project assignment
  - Project role
  - Timesheet date falling within cost rate period
- Uses left join for cost rates since not all timesheets have matching cost rate records

## Cost Rate Logic
Cost rates are matched when the timesheet date falls within the cost rate's start and end date range. If no match is found, `cost_rate` and `cost_rate_currency` will be null.

doc.cr_project.bc_absence_type.name: bc_absence_type
doc.cr_project.bc_absence_type.block_contents:
# Model: bc_absence_type

## Business Purpose
Assembles the full business concept for Absence Type at a Point In Time (PIT) of the dbt run. Enriches hub and satellite data with the deductible supply hours classification carried in the dedicated datavault satellite.

## Business Logic & Key Calculations
- Joins `hub_absence_type`, `pit_absence_type`, and `sat_absence_type` (including the `sat_absence_type_deductible_supply_hours` attributes via the PIT/BC join) to produce the current-state record per absence type.
 - Derives `is_deductible_from_supply_hours` from the `sat_absence_type_deductible_supply_hours` satellite: absence types flagged as deductible in that satellite are `true`; all others are `false`.

## Sources & Dependencies
 - `hub_absence_type`, `pit_absence_type`, `sat_absence_type`, `sat_absence_type_deductible_supply_hours` — datavault raw layer
 - Upstream to the deductible supply hours satellite: `stg_manual__absence_type_deductible_supply_hours` — manual seed staging model

## Key Fields
- `h_absence_type_sid` — hashed surrogate key
- `absence_type_bk` — natural Business Key from Workday
- `absence_name` — display name of the absence type
- `is_deductible_from_supply_hours` — boolean flag; `true` if the absence type reduces supply hours

## Update Frequency
- Updated with each dbt job run.

doc.cr_project.pit_absence_type.name: pit_absence_type
doc.cr_project.pit_absence_type.block_contents: This model takes information from the Absence Type satellites and extracts the most recent data, with Point In Time (PIT) of the runtime of the DBT project

doc.cr_project.bc_absence_type_current.name: bc_absence_type_current
doc.cr_project.bc_absence_type_current.block_contents:
# Model: bc_absence_type_current

## Business Purpose
Provides the current, deduplicated view of each absence type by selecting only the latest `as_of_date` record per `h_absence_type_sid` from `bc_absence_type`. Intended for use by downstream dimension models that require a single row per absence type.

## Business Logic & Key Calculations
- Deduplicates `bc_absence_type` using `QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY h_absence_type_sid ORDER BY as_of_date DESC) = 1`.
- Applies `IFNULL` defaults: `'ghost'` for string columns, `false` for `is_deductible_from_supply_hours`, and `'Keep'` for `deductible_from_supply_hours`.

## Sources & Dependencies
- `bc_absence_type` — business concept model

## Key Fields
- `h_absence_type_sid` — hashed surrogate key (unique in this model)
- `absence_type_bk` — natural Business Key from Workday
- `absence_name` — display name of the absence type
- `is_deductible_from_supply_hours` — boolean; `true` if the absence type reduces supply hours
- `deductible_from_supply_hours` — `Remove` if deductible, `Keep` if not

## Update Frequency
- Updated with each dbt job run.

doc.cr_project.bc_forecast_booking.name: bc_forecast_booking
doc.cr_project.bc_forecast_booking.block_contents:
# Model: bc_forecast_booking

## Business Purpose
This business concept model provides a historical view of project forecast bookings with effective date ranges. It tracks resource allocations, forecasted hours, and billing rates over time, enabling analysis of project staffing and cost projections.

## Business Logic & Key Calculations
- Deduplicates records using `ROW_NUMBER()` partitioned by `resource_forecast_bk` and `cost_rate_as_of`, keeping the latest load per effective date
- Calculates `effective_to` dates using `LEAD()` window function to create non-overlapping time ranges
- Identifies the latest deletion date per `resource_forecast_sid` using `ROW_NUMBER()` with `QUALIFY`
- Excludes all deleted records (`is_deleted = 'True'`) and their history up to and including the deletion date
- Includes recreated forecast lines: if a forecast with the same resource forecast line key is recreated after deletion, records with `effective_from` dates after the deletion date will be included

## Sources & Dependencies
- `tlnk_forecast_booking`: Transaction link containing forecast booking records with historical tracking and deletion flags

## Key Fields
- `tlnk_forecast_booking_sid`: Surrogate key for the forecast booking link
- `resource_forecast_sid`: Surrogate key for the resource forecast
- `resource_forecast_bk`: Business key for the resource forecast
- `effective_from`: Start of the validity period for this record
- `effective_to`: End of the validity period for this record (exclusive)
- `forecasted_hours`: Projected hours for the resource allocation
- `project_role_cost_rate`: Cost rate for the project role
- `contract_billing_rate`: Billing rate as per contract
- `is_deleted`: Indicates if the record has been deleted

## Update Frequency
This view is refreshed based on the underlying `tlnk_forecast_booking` table update schedule.

## Additional Notes
- Uses `mutually_exclusive_ranges` test to ensure no overlapping effective date ranges per resource forecast
- The high date default is controlled by the dbt variable `high_date`
- Custom test `record_after_deletion_check` in file `test/generic/bc_forecast_booking_records_after_deletion` validates that deletion logic correctly includes the records that is being recreated after deletion

doc.cr_project.bc_project_cost_rate.name: bc_project_cost_rate
doc.cr_project.bc_project_cost_rate.block_contents:
# Model: bc_project_cost_rate

## Business Purpose
Assembles Project Cost Rate business concept data at PIT of dbt run with overlap resolution applied.

## Business Logic & Key Calculations
- Sources data from staging layer (`stg_workday__project_cost_rate_versent_pty_ltd`)
- Generates surrogate keys for Project Cost Rate hub
- **Resolves overlapping periods** for the same project, employee, and role combination:
  - Detects overlaps by comparing consecutive period end dates with start dates
  - Groups overlapping periods together using running sum logic
  - Collapses overlapping periods by applying business rules:
    - **Start Date**: Earliest start date in overlap group
    - **End Date**: Latest end date in overlap group
    - **Cost Rate**: Lowest cost rate in overlap group
    - **Currency & Source**: First values in overlap group
    - **Load DateTime**: Most recent load time in overlap group
- Returns clean, non-overlapping Project Cost Rate records

## Usage
This model is used by:
- `int_fact_time_sheet_bks`

doc.cr_project.bc_standard_cost_rate.name: bc_standard_cost_rate
doc.cr_project.bc_standard_cost_rate.block_contents:
# Model: bc_standard_cost_rate

## Business Purpose
This model provides a business core view of standard cost rates, including the effective date ranges for each project role and currency. It enables accurate historical tracking and reporting of cost rate changes.

## Business Logic & Key Calculations
- Calculates the `effective_to` date for each cost rate record based on the next available `effective_from` date for the same project_role_bk and currency.
- Uses window functions to determine the end date of each rate period.
- Ensures that the last record for each group has a high date (`9999-12-31`) as its `effective_to`.
- Sources only the latest, non-deleted records.

## Sources & Dependencies
- Depends on the `tlnk_standard_cost_rate` model for input data.
- Upstream source: `stg_workday__standard_cost_rate`.

## Key Fields
- `project_role_bk`: Identifier for the project role.
- `currency`: Currency of the cost rate.
- `effective_from`: Start date of the cost rate period.
- `effective_to`: End date of the cost rate period.
- `standard_cost_rate`: The cost rate value.
- `record_source`: Source system for the record.
- `load_date_time`: Timestamp when the record was loaded.

doc.cr_project.hub_absence_type.name: hub_absence_type
doc.cr_project.hub_absence_type.block_contents:
# Model: hub_absence_type

## Business Purpose
Datavault hub containing all Business Keys and their hashed SIDs for the Absence Type Business Object. Serves as the primary key anchor for all absence type data in the data vault.

## Business Logic & Key Calculations
- Stores one record per unique absence type Business Key (`ABSENCE_TYPE_BK`).
- Incremental model: once an absence type is loaded, it is never removed.
- Descriptive attributes are stored in corresponding satellites.

## Sources & Dependencies
- **Source:** Workday
- Depends on: `int_dv_absence_type` (unions Leave of Absence and Time Off types)

## Key Fields
- `h_absence_type_sid` — hashed surrogate key derived from `ABSENCE_TYPE_BK`
- `absence_type_bk` — natural Business Key from Workday (Leave Type ID or Time Off ID)

## Update Frequency
- Updated with each dbt job run as new absence types are added in Workday.

## Additional Notes
- Data covers every Absence Type found in the Workday Leave of Absence and Time Off reports.
- See `sat_absence_type` for descriptive attributes.

doc.cr_project.sat_absence_type_deductib.name: sat_absence_type_deductible_supply_hours
doc.cr_project.sat_absence_type_deductib.block_contents:
# Model: sat_absence_type_deductible_supply_hours

## Business Purpose
Datavault satellite containing the controlled list of absence types that are deductible from supply hours. Loaded from a manually maintained seed file, this satellite provides the definitive mapping used to determine whether an employee absence should reduce supply hours in downstream calculations.

## Business Logic & Key Calculations
- Linked to `hub_absence_type` via `h_absence_type_sid`.
- Incremental model: new records are inserted when the payload changes (detected via `ABSENCE_TYPE_DEDUCTIBLE_SUPPLY_HOURS_HASHDIFF`).
- Only absence types that appear in this satellite are considered deductible from supply hours.

## Sources & Dependencies
- Depends on: `int_dv_absence_type_deductible_supply_hours`
- Related hub: `hub_absence_type`
- Seed file: `data/landing_manual/absence_type_deductible_supply_hours.csv`

## Key Fields
- `h_absence_type_sid` — foreign key to `hub_absence_type`
- `absence_name` — display name of the deductible absence type as it appears in Workday
- `absence_type_deductible_supply_hours_hashdiff` — change detection hash over the payload

## Update Frequency
- Updated manually when deductible absence types are added or changed in Workday.

## Additional Notes
- Used downstream by `bc_absence_type` to populate `is_deductible_from_supply_hours` and `deductible_from_supply_hours`.
- See `dim_absence_type` for the gold layer representation.

# Model: hub_customer_contract

## Business Purpose
This datavault hub contains all Business Keys and their hashed SIDs for the Customer Contract Business Object. Data is for every Customer Contract found in the Workday Customer Contract Lines extract.

## Business Logic & Key Calculations
- Contains the Primary Key for each Customer Contract ID.
- Data itself is contained with corresponding satellites (sats).

## Sources & Dependencies
- Workday Customer Contract Lines extract

## Key Fields
- Customer Contract ID (Business Key)
- SID (Surrogate ID)

## Update Frequency
- Updated as new Customer Contracts are added to Workday.

## Additional Notes
- See related satellite documentation below.

doc.cr_project.sat_customer_contract.name: sat_customer_contract
doc.cr_project.sat_customer_contract.block_contents:
# Model: sat_customer_contract

## Business Purpose
This satellite contains all Customer Contract names obtained from Workday.

## Business Logic & Key Calculations
- Stores descriptive attributes for Customer Contracts.

## Sources & Dependencies
- Workday Customer Contract Lines extract
- Linked to hub_customer_contract

## Key Fields
- Customer Contract Name
- Customer Contract ID (Business Key)

## Update Frequency
- Updated as new Customer Contracts are added to Workday.

## Additional Notes
- Works in conjunction with hub_customer_contract.

This model creates a SID generation layer for the int_lnk_opportunity model, in preparation for lnk_opportunity

We replaced the `left join` with an `inner join` to enforce stricter mapping integrity between Salesforce values and Workday cost centres.  
To prevent data loss from unmapped combinations, we introduced ghost values in the mapping seed file 
for unmatched Region–Business Unit–Practice combinations.

This ensures complete and consistent mappings while maintaining join integrity.

## Update Frequency

- Used for linking standard cost rate business keys in Data Vault architecture.

doc.cr_project.tlnk_employee_absence.name: tlnk_employee_absence
doc.cr_project.tlnk_employee_absence.block_contents:
# Model: tlnk_employee_absence

## Business Purpose
Raw Data Vault transactional link that records employee absence events, linking employee absences to employees and absence types with temporal validity periods.

## Business Logic & Key Calculations
- Immutable transactional link (append-only)
- Captures absence records with effectivity dates (START_DATE) and end dates

## Sources & Dependencies
- **Source**: `int_tlnk_employee_absence`
- **Related Hubs**: `hub_employee_absence`, `hub_employee`, `hub_absence_type`

## Key Fields
- `TLNK_EMPLOYEE_ABSENCE_SID`: Primary key (MD5 hash of EMPLOYEE_ABSENCE_BK, START_DATE, LOAD_DATE_TIME)
- `H_EMPLOYEE_ABSENCE_SID`: Hub reference for the absence event
- `H_EMPLOYEE_SID`: Hub reference for the employee
- `H_ABSENCE_TYPE_SID`: Hub reference for the absence type
- `START_DATE`: Absence effectivity start date
- `END_DATE`: Absence end date
- `STATUS`: Absence status
- `UNIT_OF_TIME`: Unit of time for the absence (e.g., hours, days)
- `UNIT_QUANTITY`: Quantity of the unit of time
- `LOAD_DATE_TIME`: Record load timestamp
- `RECORD_SOURCE`: Source system identifier

doc.cr_project.stg_manual_actuals_tracke.name: stg_manual_actuals_tracker
doc.cr_project.stg_manual_actuals_tracke.block_contents:
This view obtains data from the Manual S3 CSV upload 'actuals_tracker.csv'
      
      Finance have a process of approving actuals for a month.
      If a month's actuals have not been approved, and is in a incomplete month, we dont want to include these Actuals in calculations

      The Actuals Tracker allows for the filtering of months in Actuals and Forecast models being PRE and POST this demarkation month.

      After the file is modified in S3 bucket, an SQL query should be created with 
      ```sql
        CREATE OR REPLACE EXTERNAL TABLE EXT_ACTUALS_TRACKER
            LOCATION = @MANUAL_FILES_API_STAGE/
            AUTO_REFRESH = FALSE
            PATTERN = "manual_uploads/actuals_tracker/data/actuals_tracker(?:.*)(?:.csv)"
            FILE_FORMAT = CSV_FMT;

        GRANT OWNERSHIP ON EXTERNAL TABLE EXT_ACTUALS_TRACKER TO ROLE REPORTING_ANALYTICS_DBA;
        GRANT SELECT ON EXTERNAL TABLE EXT_ACTUALS_TRACKER TO ROLE REPORTING_ANALYTICS_PROD_SUPPORT_DBA;
     ```
     See full implementation context and history in:
     [EAG-1745](https://versent.atlassian.net/browse/EAG-1745)
     [EAG-1200](https://versent.atlassian.net/jira/software/projects/EAG/boards/358?selectedIssue=EAG-3200)

     This model includes a recency test specified in manual_schema.yml to ensure data freshness based on the file_timestamp column.
     The threshold has been updated to 360 days to reflect the expected update frequency of the source file, with the change in the value of interval
     This change is linked to [EAG-3193](https://versent.atlassian.net/jira/software/projects/EAG/boards/358?selectedIssue=EAG-3193)
     Related dbt docs here: https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-utils/tree/1.3.0/#recency-source

- Contains only absence types that should reduce supply hours.
- Downstream models join on `absence_type_bk` or `absence_name` to determine whether an absence should be deducted from supply hours.

## Sources & Dependencies
- Seed file: `data/landing_manual/absence_type_deductible_supply_hours.csv`
- Used downstream by `dim_absence_type` and supply hours / utilisation calculations.

## Key Fields
- `absence_type_bk` — the absence type business key as it appears in Workday
- `absence_name` — the display name of the absence type

## Update Frequency
- Updated manually when new deductible absence types are introduced in Workday.

## Additional Notes
- Related ticket: introduces a controlled mapping to replace ad-hoc Power BI logic.
- See `dim_absence_type` for the downstream usage of this lookup.

doc.cr_project.snapshot_standard_cost_ra.block_contents:
# Model: snapshot_standard_cost_rate

## Business Purpose
This snapshot tracks changes to the standard cost rate for project roles in Workday over time. It enables historical analysis and auditing of cost rate changes for project roles.

## Business Logic & Key Calculations
- Captures all records from the staging model `stg_workday__standard_cost_rate`.
- `standard_cost_rate_bk` (a composite key of Project_Role_ID, Effective_From, and Currency) is used as the unique key.
- Follows a timestamp strategy to record changes whenever the effective date or other tracked fields are updated.

## Sources & Dependencies
- Source: `stg_workday__standard_cost_rate` (staging model for Workday standard cost rate data)
- Depends on the external Workday data source and the staging transformation logic.

## Key Fields
- `Project_Role_ID`: Unique identifier for the project role.
- `Effective_From`: Date when the cost rate became effective.
- `Project_Role`: Name of the project role.
- `Standard_Cost_Rate`: Standard cost rate for the project role.
- `record_source`: Source file for the record.
- `load_date_time`: Timestamp when the record was loaded.

## Update Frequency
- Updated whenever the source data in Workday changes and the dbt snapshot is run (typically daily or as scheduled).

## Additional Notes
- Ensures historical tracking of cost rate changes for compliance and reporting.
- Follows dbt and project style guide conventions for naming, structure, and documentation.

doc.cr_project.snapshot_time_sheet.name: snapshot_time_sheet
doc.cr_project.snapshot_time_sheet.block_contents:
## Overview

The `time_sheet` snapshot tracks historical changes to timesheet records sourced from the `stg_workday_time_block_audit` model. This snapshot enables auditing and analysis of timesheet data over time, capturing every change to key business attributes.

For reporting purposes, this snapshot also joins and includes the IDs for project role and practice, as these are not present in the original source but are required for downstream analytics and business consumption.

## Purpose

- Maintain a full history of timesheet records for compliance and auditability.
- Detect and record changes to important timesheet fields, such as hours worked, billing rates, and statuses.
- Support reporting on both current and historical states of timesheet data.

## Change Detection Strategy
This snapshot uses the **check strategy** with a set of business-critical columns. A new record is created whenever any of these columns change for a given timesheet key (`TIMESHEET_BK`). 
The snapshot records the validity period for each version using `dbt_valid_from` and `dbt_valid_to` fields.
The snaphost use 'hard_deleted = `ignore` because the Time_Block_Audit report is using high water mark and it also uses is_deleted field to identify deletion.

### Tracked Columns

- `TASK_CODE`
- `TOTAL_HOURS__TIME_TRACKING`
- `BILLABLE_HOURS`
- `BILLING_CURRENCY`
- `BILLABLE_RATE`
- `BILLING_STATUS`
- `REVENUE_STATUS`
- `INVOICE_NUMBER`
- `OVERRIDE_RATE`
- `CALCULATED_DATE`
- `IS_DELETED`

## Additional Notes

- The snapshot is refreshed as part of the dbt run process.
- Ensure that the source staging model (`stg_workday_time_block_audit`) is up to date for accurate snapshotting.
- For more information, refer to the [dbt snapshot documentation](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/snapshots).

in this interface, as they do not exist in the database.

### Graph Exploration
You can click the blue icon on the bottom-right corner of the page to view the lineage graph of your models.

On model pages, you'll see the immediate parents and children of the model you're exploring. By clicking the `Expand`

Once expanded, you'll be able to use the `--select` and `--exclude` model selection syntax to filter the
models in the graph. For more information on model selection, check out the [dbt docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/model-selection-syntax).

Note that you can also right-click on models to interactively filter and explore the graph.

model.dbt_project_evaluator.fct_root_mod.name: fct_root_models
model.dbt_project_evaluator.fct_root_mod.description: This table shows each model with 0 direct parents.
model.dbt_project_evaluator.fct_root_mod.raw_code:
-- this model finds cases where a model has 0 direct parents, likely due to a lack of source or ref function

{% if execute %}
{% set metric_flow_time_spine_names = graph.nodes.values()
     | selectattr("resource_type", "equalto", "model") 
     | rejectattr("time_spine", "none") 
     | map(attribute = "name") 
     | join("', '")
%}
{% endif %}

with model_relationships as (
    select  
        *
    from {{ ref('int_all_dag_relationships') }}
    where child_resource_type = 'model'
    -- only filter out excluded children nodes
        -- filtering parents could result in incorrectly flagging nodes that depend on excluded nodes
    and not child_is_excluded
    -- exclude required time spine
    {% if metric_flow_time_spine_names %}
    and child not in ('{{ metric_flow_time_spine_names }}')
    {% endif %}
),

final as (
    select
        child
    from model_relationships
    group by 1
    having max(distance) = 0
)

select * from final

{{ filter_exceptions() }}

**Source:** Salesforce

# Model: dim_client

## Business Purpose
Contains information about Clients. Serves as the primary location for all client-related information.

## Business Logic & Key Calculations
- Incremental model: if a Client is removed from the source system, it remains within this Dimension.
- Point in Time (PIT) is the time of the dbt job run, using the most recent information.

## Sources & Dependencies
- Source system for Clients
- Used by downstream reporting and fact models

## Key Fields
- Client ID
- Client Name
- Timestamps (for PIT)

## Update Frequency
- Updated with each dbt job run or as new Clients are added/modified.

## Additional Notes
- Ensures historical Clients are retained for reporting and analysis. Client dimension semantic model.
